title: Patchummuck (Tom's Creek)
summary: Patchummuck is connected with a boundary point at the head of Tom's Creek on Hashamomuk Neck in Southold.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Tom's Creek / Hashamomuck Pond landscape point based on Tooker location; not an exact historical boundary coordinate.
history_content: The placename belongs to the Hashamomuk Neck boundary landscape, where creek, pond, and neck names intersect. Boundary details appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as a turning aside place or place where it turns aside, referring to a boundary line changing direction at the head of the creek. A recorded variant is Pashimamsk.

Why Place Names Matter

“Places are named for all kinds of reasons; reminders of home, a link to a homeland, to erase what was there before, and many more.”

— Dan David, Traditional Land Use (2018), Opening paragraph
whereintheworld_content: Approximate/general point near the Tom's Creek and Hashamomuck Pond landscape in Southold. This is not an exact historical boundary coordinate.
